leading_positions.synthesis: Both back targeted protein degradation with the same trio (Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli) and a citation built on PROTACs and chemically induced proximity to E3 ligases. Both describe a designable, catalytic, event-driven mechanism with independent reproduction and many clinical candidates. Both also concede that no PROTAC drug is approved, that the cereblon/thalidomide molecular-glue lineage (Handa, Ito, Kim, Sakamoto, Gray) has distinct credit, and that the three-name cap leaves out contributors. They differ in emphasis: Aili stresses the chemical design principle and offers narrowing the citation, while Chabes states that a PROTAC-only trio omits the part of the field with the most patient benefit. Chabes also raises Sakamoto and Handa as alternatives for the third name.

Both back biomolecular phase separation with the same trio (Hyman, Brangwynne, Rosen). They share the view that the 2009 P-granule droplet work and Rosen's multivalent reconstitution give a dated, physical-chemical origin separable from later refinements. They also share the main reservation: physiological relevance in vivo is argued case by case, there is no therapeutic payoff yet, and Pappu and Mittag are excluded. The citation wordings differ slightly: one speaks of membraneless compartments organized by multivalent interactions, the other of a physical-chemical principle of intracellular organisation. Both name B068 as an alternative.

Both back nitrogenase structure and mechanism with Rees and Seefeldt, but they differ on the third laureate: Brzezinski names Dean, Zou names Einsle. Both note that the catalytic mechanism of N2 reduction is unresolved, so the citation must be limited to structure and cofactor chemistry or the established framework. Both flag crowded credit among Rees, Dean, Einsle, Seefeldt and Ribbe. Brzezinski discloses that his preference partly reflects his interest in biological energy conversion. Zou's statement cites B033 as his own first choice although his stated configuration is B009; this internal inconsistency should be clarified.

Single supporter of base editing with Liu, Komor and Gaudelli, valued as a conceptually simple new chemical tool with tractable attribution. He lists the short clinical record, overlap with the 2020 CRISPR prize, the unresolved Kondo and Nishida Target-AID priority question, and the possible later relevance of prime editing (B038) as reservations.

Single supporter of palladium-catalysed C-N cross-coupling with Buchwald and Hartwig as a two-person citation, with about thirty years of confirmation and clean attribution. He lists closeness to the 2010 cross-coupling prize and the earlier Kosugi tin-amide coupling as reservations, and says he cannot fully verify the priority record.

areas_of_agreement: The eight first-choice configurations are split among five ballots (B068 two, B003 two, B009 two, B024 one, B004 one); no ballot has a majority of five, and no member's configuration contains more than one prize part.

B068 is named as an alternative by five members (Aqvist, Linke, Somfai, Sparr, Zou) in addition to its two first-choice supporters, so seven of eight members explicitly place it in their first choice or alternatives. This counts only explicit alternatives lists.
B003 is named as an alternative by Aili, Aqvist, Brzezinski and Chabes in addition to its two first-choice supporters, so six members explicitly place it in their first choice or alternatives.

Every member states a weakness in their own first choice; most tie it to attribution under the three-person cap, and all eight configurations were proposed with a stated limitation rather than as uncontested.
No member reports a specific disclosed conflict with any credited candidate.
scientific_disputes: B003: whether the core physical-chemical discovery (demixing driven by multivalency) can be separated from contested in vivo claims about overexpression artefacts and the line between true phase separation and other assemblies. Linke and Sparr support the prize but Aili notes it is debated, and several members rank it second or third.
B009: whether a nitrogenase citation can be worded around structure and cofactor chemistry when the N2 reduction mechanism and catalytic intermediates remain unresolved (Brzezinski, Zou).

B024 versus 2020: whether base editing is a distinct chemical discovery or an extension of CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing, and whether it is better considered with prime editing (B038) (Aqvist; Aili notes the central advance is an engineered protein fusion).
B004 versus 2010: whether C-N coupling, with a different mechanistic bottleneck (reductive elimination from amido complexes), is distinct from the C-C cross-coupling prize (Somfai).
B068: whether PROTACs and molecular glues are one scientific lineage (induced proximity to E3 ligases) or two with distinct origins (Chabes, Aili).
B023: Linke notes the overlap with earlier computational prizes (1998 DFT, 2013 multiscale) is not negligible, and Sparr asks whether recent prizes reduce room for B025 or B032.
attribution_disputes: B068: the third name beside Crews and Deshaies is Ciulli in both first-choice configurations, but Chabes says Handa or Sakamoto (first small-molecule PROTAC) could instead be named; the glue lineage (Handa, Ito, Kim, Sakamoto, Gray) is excluded from both trios.
B003: both first-choice configurations use Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen; the open question is whether Pappu or Mittag should replace Rosen, given sequence-encoded phase behaviour.

B009: the two B009 trios differ (Rees, Dean, Seefeldt versus Rees, Einsle, Seefeldt); Ribbe is not named in either, and Brzezinski and Zou both flag that any trio leaves out someone with a serious claim.
B024: whether Kondo and Nishida's independent Target-AID work should displace Komor or Gaudelli in a Liu-centred trio.
B004: how to acknowledge Kosugi's 1983 tin-amide coupling as a precursor without crediting it; Somfai cannot fully verify the priority record.
maturity_disputes: B068: no PROTAC drug is approved, so clinical validation is incomplete and 2026 may be early (Aili, Chabes), against the case that the mechanism is molecularly defined and reproduced across many targets and E3 ligases.
B003: the field is over fifteen years old but physiological relevance is still argued case by case and there is no therapeutic payoff yet (Linke, Sparr).
B024: about ten years old, a short clinical record, and open issues in bystander and off-target editing (Aqvist).

B009 and B004: both are described as mature, with about three decades of independent confirmation; B009's open question is mechanistic completeness rather than timing, and B004's is closeness to an earlier prize.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Brzezinski discloses that his preference for B009 partly reflects his own interest in biological energy conversion; he works on cytochrome c oxidase, not nitrogenase, and no collaboration with B009 candidates is shown in his profile.
Aqvist discloses a professional connection to Arieh Warshel and says he would declare it for computational candidates such as B023 and B032; he reports no connection to B024, B068 or B003.
Zou is a Stockholm University colleague of Brzezinski, and both support B009; Zou states this is not a personal tie to any candidate.

Linke, Somfai and Sparr share a Lund affiliation; no shortlisted candidate is linked to Lund in the member statements. Sparr notes her membrane and amyloid work is close to phase separation and lipid nanoparticle science and Aili notes research overlap with Sparr on peptide self-assembly; both state these are not recusal issues.
questions_for_round2: B003: can the committee write a citation for the physical-chemical principle of liquid-liquid demixing and multivalency that stands without asserting that specific condensates are phase-separated in vivo, and does it then still choose Rosen over Pappu or Mittag as third name?
B068: should PROTACs and molecular glues be one prize or two, and if one, which three names (Crews, Deshaies, with Ciulli, Handa or Sakamoto) fit the citation, given that no PROTAC is approved?
B009: given the unresolved N2 reduction mechanism, is a structure-and-cofactor citation sufficient, and should the third name beside Rees and Seefeldt be Dean or Einsle, with Ribbe's claim addressed?

B024: does the committee consider base editing separable from the 2020 CRISPR prize, how should Kondo and Nishida's Target-AID priority be weighed against Komor and Gaudelli, and would prime editing (B038) change the timing?

B004 and B023: do closeness to the 2010 cross-coupling prize and to the 1998 and 2013 computational prizes weigh decisively against these candidates, and how should Kosugi's precursor work be treated?

Maturity criterion: does the committee weight reproducibility and clean attribution (B004, B009) above conceptual reach (B003, B068) when no ballot has majority support, and what evidence would let members move from their first choice to a fallback?
Zou: please clarify whether B009 or B033 is your first choice, given that your statement calls B033 your own first choice while your configuration is B009.
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 shows a three-way split of first choices among B068, B003 and B009 (two each), plus single supporters of B024 and B004. B068 is the most frequently named alternative (five members), and every first-choice supporter listed a maturity or attribution reservation about their own preference. Four of the five first-choice ballots share an unresolved third-name or citation-wording question, so round 2 will be about citation design as much as ranking. As chair, I am a first-choice supporter of B003 and have tried to summarize all positions on equal terms.
